key_insight: Trivalent (degree-3) planar architectures can support scalable surface-code lattice surgery with lower resource overhead than standard four-valent schemes.
engineering_relevance: This reduces qubit and two-qubit gate requirements, making fault-tolerant logical operations more practical for near-term planar hardware such as fluxonium-based platforms.
method: Developed scalable lattice-surgery circuit constructions for trivalent planar connectivity.
Compared resource scaling against the four-valent measurement scheme.
Simulated logical fidelity for experimentally realistic fluxonium architecture targets.
evidence_signal: Abstract reports theoretical resource savings of O(d) qubits and O(d) two-qubit gates, plus simulations suggesting up to ~25% improvement in logical fidelity at distance three.
watch_item: The reported advantage is based on distance-three simulations and architecture-specific assumptions, so performance may vary for larger codes or different hardware constraints.
paper_title: Towards logical entanglement creation in trivalent planar architectures
